GARY BETTENHAUSEN of Tinley Park, Il., has a different background from his teammate. The son of great
driver Tony Bettenhausen drove USAC stocks, midgets and sprints, taking two championships in the latter
division, in 1969 and last year. He finished seventh in USAC Championship points last year, earning
$101,715. He has three Trail wins to his credit, the most recent coming in April of this year at Trenton,
N.J. At 30 he now has one of the best rides on the circuit, the Penske McLaren M16B Offy. Gary has gone
through a transition from a good driver to one of the best, with the help of Penske.

BOBBY UNSER, who won the Tony Bettenhausen Classic here last August, has become the hot setup on the USAC Championship Trail. In the three events be-
fore the Rex Mays Classic this year he has sat on the pole three timesl Each time he shattered the track qualifying record. At Phoenix in March he also won
the 150-mile event. A mechanical malfunction stopped his runaway at Trenton in April. He turned the qualifications for the Indianapolis 500 into a route when
he qualified at an average speed of 195.940 mph with one lap at 196.678. Though all of the cars on the Trail this year are faster, the Dan Gurney-owned
Olsonite Eagle Offy is a step ahead of the rest. Meticulous preparation and extremely clean aerodynamics help account for the mechanical end while nearly
two decades of racing experience account for Unser's exceptional ability at the new higher speeds — a truly winning combination.
